title: Retrieving Data from a Canister
section: 40. Building DApps on ICP with a React Frontend
summary: Adds the Read step of CRUD. A query function readNotes converts the stored List to an array and returns it; in App.jsx a useEffect with an empty dependency array calls an async fetchData on first load and puts the result in state. Also fixes the display order by prepending new notes in the frontend to match the backend.

concepts.heading: State of play
points: Notes created in the UI already reach the canister's notes list (visible in the debug output), but nothing reads them back, so the UI loses them on refresh.

concepts.heading: The readNotes query function
points: Declare it as public query func readNotes() : async [Note]. It takes no input.
The query keyword marks a function that only reads state. Query calls skip consensus and respond much faster than update calls, so use them for any read-only method.
Return type is an array of Note, written [Note], not a List. Arrays map closely to JavaScript arrays, so the data arrives on the frontend as a plain array of objects with title and content.
The backend still stores a List because pushing and later removing items is cheaper than on an array (arrays are serialised and expensive to rebuild on chain). Convert only when returning.
List.toArray(notes) takes one argument, the list, and returns an array. Motoko's base library has fewer utility functions than JS or Python, so finding the right one means reading the module docs.
After editing main.mo, run dfx deploy so the generated declarations include readNotes.

concepts.heading: Loading data on first render with useEffect
points: useState re-renders the component on updates, but a hook is needed to run code when the page first loads. useEffect runs after a component renders, including the first render.
First argument: a function to run (arrow function, no inputs). A console.log inside is a quick way to confirm when it fires.
The function passed to useEffect cannot itself be async, so define a separate async function fetchData and call it from inside the effect.
fetchData: const notesArray = await dkeeper_backend.readNotes(); then setNotes(notesArray). The await is needed because canister calls return promises.
Trap: setNotes changes state, which re-renders App, which triggers useEffect again, which fetches again, endlessly. The console shows the log repeating.
Fix: pass a second argument, a dependency array. useEffect re-runs only when a listed value changes; an empty array [] means run once, after the first render.
Result: add notes, refresh, and they stay, because they are read from the canister each load.

concepts.heading: Fixing the order
points: Backend push prepends, so after a refresh the newest note appears first, but the frontend's addNote appended new notes to the end, so the order flipped on reload.
Newest-first matches how note apps normally behave and keeps new items visible at the top of a long list.
Change addNote's returned array from [...prevNotes, newNote] to [newNote, ...prevNotes]. Now the UI order matches the canister order before and after refresh.

concepts.heading: Remaining gap
points: Delete only changes frontend state, so a refreshed page re-fetches the deleted note from the canister. Handled in the next lesson.

task.name: Read notes back from the canister
task.starting_point: Project from the previous lesson where createNote stores notes in a List but the UI never loads them.
task.goal: Notes persist across page refreshes and appear newest first.
steps: Add public query func readNotes() : async [Note] returning List.toArray(notes).
Write async function fetchData that awaits dkeeper_backend.readNotes() and calls setNotes.
Observe (optionally) the infinite loop by removing the [] and then restore it.
Add notes, refresh and confirm they persist in the same order.
task.expected_result: Refreshing keeps all notes, with the latest at the top before and after reload.
task.reference_repo_path: Section 40 - Building DApps on ICP with a React Frontend/40.03 Retrieving Data from a Canister/dkeeper/src/dkeeper_frontend/src/App.jsx

pitfalls: Omitting the [] dependency array, which creates an endless fetch/render loop.
Making the useEffect callback itself async.
Forgetting await on the canister call, so a Promise is stored in state.
Returning the List directly instead of converting to an array.
Appending on the frontend while the backend prepends, flipping the order on refresh.
(Extra) In React StrictMode dev builds effects run twice on mount; that is not the infinite loop.
